complexity.instructions: How hard is the work this card describes to get right? Judge the work, not the length of the card.
criteria: Mechanical: a rename, configuration churn, or repetitive edits whose shape is obvious from the start
Standard: an ordinary feature or fix of normal size, with a clear approach
Hard: architecture, a refactor that cuts across the codebase, a subtle bug, or an approach that is not yet clear

creativity.instructions: How much of this work's value rests on taste and design choices, rather than on a shape the task already dictates?
criteria: Little: the shape of the result is dictated, and there is a single reasonable way to build it
Some: there is some room for design choices, but the shape of the result is mostly set
Much: taste is the deliverable, as in visual or user-facing design, the shape of an interface others will call, or naming

autonomy.instructions: Will this work run through many dependent steps over a long stretch, with little chance for anyone to steer it midway, rather than finishing in a single focused pass?

speed_sensitivity.instructions: Is this work a tight iteration loop, where how quickly each turn comes back matters more than anything else about it?

cost_sensitivity.instructions: Is this bulk, high-volume work, or work that is only worth doing if it can be done cheaply?

verification_criticality.instructions: Is honestly running and reporting the checks the actual deliverable of this work, so that the check is the point, rather than an edit whose correctness is easy to eyeball or re-run later?
